text: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the hottest planet.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only one known to host life.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and is known as the Red Planet.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is famous for its ring system.
Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and rotates on its side.
Neptune is the eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun.
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometers.
The capital of France is Paris.
The capital of Japan is Tokyo.
The capital of Australia is Canberra.
The Nile is often cited as the longest river in the world.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
Russia is the largest country in the world by area.
India is the most populous country in the world.
The capital of Canada is Ottawa.
The chemical symbol for gold is Au.
The chemical symbol for sodium is Na.
The chemical formula for water is H2O.
The speed of light is approximately 299792 kilometers per second.
Hydrogen is the lightest element.
Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.
A pH value of 7 is considered neutral.
Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
The atomic number of carbon is 6.
The mitochondria is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
The adult human body has 206 bones.
DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid.
The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
Red blood cells carry oxygen through the body.
Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplast.
The human heart has four chambers.
Insulin is the hormone that regulates blood sugar.
The blue whale is the largest mammal on Earth.
Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes.
CPU stands for Central Processing Unit.
RAM stands for Random Access Memory.
HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol.
The Python programming language was created by Guido van Rossum.
The binary number system uses base 2.
HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
A byte consists of 8 bits.
SQL stands for Structured Query Language.
The time complexity of binary search is O(log n).
Linux was created by Linus Torvalds.
